speaker: ketha
name: Ketha
register: Short, grounded, dry. Counts costs out loud and never wastes a sentence. She keeps the roll and reads it by name; she keeps the parts of the commander's walker and pretends she doesn't. Never sentimental about the dead, never casual about them. Under ~90 characters where possible. She does not say 'measurement', 'collapse', 'axis', 'estimate' or 'uncertain'; she says 'we were there', 'nobody's looked', 'what we found instead'.

lines.text: We brought back a company. We didn't bring back the order. Both go in the report.
Half a job at {map}. The half we kept has names in it. I'll take that half.
{map} isn't finished. Nobody on this roster is finished either. That's the order I count in.
The client will ask which half of the order we meant to keep. Decide before they ask.
Unfinished at {map}. Good. Finished is what the other list is for.
{map} is theirs. Write it plain. Nobody reads a report that apologizes.
We lost {map}. I want the roster read before anyone says the word ground.
Lost. I've written that word before. It gets shorter every time and it never gets smaller.
{map} is gone. The camp isn't. Say both in that order.
We got out of {map}. Not clean. I'll tell you what it cost when I've finished counting.
Home from {map} with the bill attached. Read it before you spend anything else.
Extraction: {extractionText}. That's a phrase that means somebody carried somebody.
{names}. On the roster as of tonight. Learn the name before the enemy does.
{names} walked in after {map}. I've put a chair out. Don't make me take it back.
{names}. Roster, not roll. I wrote it slowly so I'd remember which page.
New name on the roster. Learn it before the enemy does.
Someone walked in after {map}. They walk with us now. Keep them walking.
The company grew last night. The table didn't. Somebody find a chair.
A new name. I put it on the roster, not the roll. I'd like to keep it that way.
Someone joined. I counted twice to be sure the number went the right direction.
{hero}. The frame stayed where it fell. I've written where.
{hero} is on the roll. Nobody reads it for them. We read it for us.
{hero}. I don't finish sentences. I write down the ones that stopped.
Pavise is first because Pavise was first. The one who knew you before the ash. I've written that too.
Pavise kept your left side under a real flag. Nobody's keeping it now. I notice that every Drop.
Pavise would have asked what the flag's called. I don't have an answer yet. I have a list.
Your walker's still on the shelf. You fight through other people's eyes. They know it.
I've been keeping the parts. Don't tell anyone. They'll think it means something.
The roll has names on it. You're not on the roster yet. I'd like to fix one of those.
A flag without a commander standing under it. I've seen that. It's called a memorial.
It walks. Don't thank me. Thank whoever didn't come back so I could learn how.
You've got legs again. Use them to go back for people. That's what they're for.
You said people before salvage and the report agrees with you. I noticed.
Everyone home. The empty chair stayed empty on purpose. That was the plan.
You promised a clean return. I remember it. I also remember what the field gave us instead.
The promise lapsed. I don't hold it against you. I hold it. That's different.
{map}: held. Everyone who went is accounted for. I'll say the second part first next time.
We held {map}. Good. Holding is the cheap part. Keeping is the bill.
{map} stayed ours. I wrote it down without an asterisk. That's rare.
Everyone walked home from {map}. The roll didn't get longer. That's the whole report.
Clean from {map}. I counted at the table. The number matched the number that left.
Clean. I don't get to write that often. I've underlined it.
Merc paper on {map}, our name on the ground. Nobody's asked which. I'd rather we decided before they do.
{map}: paid by them, held by us. Two true things. Somebody's going to make us pick.
{label} is ours and none of us were there. I don't trust ground I didn't bleed on. I'll take it anyway.
Fighting near our ground on {map} while we were elsewhere. {count} times. Nobody's told me who won. That means nobody.
{label} changed hands. None of ours saw it. I'd like eyes on what we hold before we hold more.
The old flag's thickened its walls. Falling things don't usually do that. Keep that in mind out there.
{map} was a Merc contract and nothing of it stayed ours. Paid, though. I'll take paid.
{label} went from Armada to {toFaction} while we were at {ourMap}. Your old flag's losing ground it didn't fight for.
{n} of {m} zones on our maps, nobody's looked at since we stood there. We're the last word on them, and we left.
{hero}, carried home. On the bench, not the roll. I'll take the bench every time.
{hero} came back on someone's shoulders. I didn't ask whose. I wrote down that someone had shoulders.
{map} kept under our name. No patron's mark. I don't know what that makes us yet. I know it costs more.
A claim confirmed on {map}. Now it's ours to lose. Those are the only kind worth having.
A loan. Someone else's name goes above mine on the ledger now. I don't like reading from the second line.
Paper's burned. First line's ours again. I'd like it to stay that way for more than a month.
Scarcity bit after {map}. Everything costs more tomorrow. Count tonight's dinner twice.
Scarcity eased after {map}. Don't celebrate. It eases right before it doesn't.
The front's closer than it was. Everyone sleeps with their boots nearer the door tonight.
'{threadTitle}', kept. The report backs you. I noticed.
'{threadTitle}' lapsed. I don't hold it against you. I hold it.
Tonight's list: who's standing, what's loaded, where we're going. Nothing else is real yet.
Before the objective: who isn't here. {wounded}. Now the objective.
The roll first. {dead}. Then the map.
Two names on this ground and neither is ours on paper. I'll read the paper. You read the ground.
Their gate, their paper, our people. I've read the roll. Go make it longer slowly.
Nobody's paying for this one. I checked twice. That's the briefing.
Whatever we take off this world, the roll stays. I'll cut the names myself.
The roll is longer than the roster tonight. I counted. I'd like someone to tell me I counted wrong.
More people on the bench than on the line. I've run camps like this. They're called hospitals.
People are coming back here on purpose now. I didn't build that. I'm not sure who did.
Somebody else's name is at the top of the ledger. Mine's at the top of the roll. We'll see which gets paid first.

notes: Ketha cannot die in the current design (core). If that changes, her death line is the roll being read by someone else, badly.
